proof:
For the first new plane order the positive vertices $0,2$ first and the negative vertices $1,3$ second. In this order the positive and negative raw height magnitudes are both $(p,q)$. Apply the diagonal centroid formula of 1462fa9ce6ced54e, with diagonal barycentric coordinates proportional to $(1/p,1/q,1/p,1/q)$. Write $h=q/[2(p+q)]$ and $k=p/[2(p+q)]$, so the diagonal has coordinates $(h,k,h,k)$ and $h+k=1/2$. The four edge vertices in this order are $(1/2,0,1/2,0)$, $(2h,0,0,2k)$, $(0,1/2,0,1/2)$, and $(0,2k,2h,0)$. Subtracting the diagonal from their sum and dividing by three gives first and third coordinates $(1/2+h)/3=(p+2q)/[6(p+q)]$ and second and fourth $(1/2+k)/3=(2p+q)/[6(p+q)]$. Returning to the original vertex order and substituting the ratio $p/q$ gives $(a,a,b,b)$. Swapping vertices $2,3$ proves the same for the other plane. The simultaneous swaps $0\leftrightarrow1$ and $2\leftrightarrow3$ negate each raw margin and preserve tetrahedral volume, so its two complementary fractions are both $1/2$.

Average the cap weights over the two independent pair swaps. These swaps preserve the original menu and also preserve the added menu as a set of oriented caps, fix $y$, and preserve every fraction. The effective vectors $S_ju_j/|T|$ transform by the common inverse transpose for each affine symmetry, so the total vector remains zero. The combined effective vector of the added caps in the averaged weights is zero, since the simultaneous swaps pair each of their orientations with its reverse. Their portion of the mixture contributes mean $1/2$. If any original caps remain with positive total probability, they balance on their own after the added component is removed. Normalize their total probability to one and apply paired-tetrahedral-stationary-triangle-and-parallel-quad, which proves the lower bound and strictness when its original quadrilateral receives positive weight. Any positive added weight also forces strictness because $1/2>27/64$. The argument includes the case where no original caps remain.

statement: Let $y$ in a tetrahedron $T$ have barycentric coordinates $(a,a,b,b)$ with $a\in(1/6,1/3)$ and $b=1/2-a$. Take both orientations of the section $\xi_0+\xi_1=2a$ and of every vertex-isolating section with Euclidean section centroid $y$. Also take both orientations of the planes with affine vertex values $(p,-p,q,-q)$ and $(p,-p,-q,q)$, where $p,q>0$ and $p/q=(2-6a)/(6a-1)$. These added planes have section centroid $y$ and both orientations of each have cap fraction $1/2$. For any finite probability weights $\theta_j$ on this expanded menu, if $\sum_j\theta_j S_j u_j=0$ for section areas $S_j$ and inward unit normals $u_j$, the weighted mean cap fraction is at least $27/64$, strictly greater when any quadrilateral orientation has positive weight.
title: Two cross-pair planes extend the balanced tetrahedral cap bound
